subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `openclaw models status --probe --all` as the canonical configured-model health check, or fold this into a different model/fallback validation workflow?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear in source, but it adds a new live CLI probe mode with cost, rate-limit, provider-error, JSON contract, and overlap decisions that automation should not settle.

options.title: Approve status-level all-model probe
options.body: Implement `--probe --all` behind the existing status command, preserving current one-model behavior by default and documenting cost, output, filtering, and proof expectations.

options.title: Fold into fallback/migration diagnostics
options.body: Keep this issue open but redirect the implementation toward the fallback-chain or staged model-migration workflow if maintainers want one broader validation surface.

options.title: Decline core CLI expansion
options.body: Close this direction only if maintainers decide external monitoring plus existing provider auth probes are sufficient for configured-model validation.

recommendation.title: Approve status-level all-model probe
recommendation.body: Implement `--probe --all` behind the existing status command, preserving current one-model behavior by default and documenting cost, output, filtering, and proof expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and most heavily maintains the current models status/probe surface, so he is the best routing owner for the product-contract choice.
